newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KOK PLAYS DOWN ELECTION EFFECT ON EU TREATY TALKS.
newsitem.headline: KOK PLAYS DOWN ELECTION EFFECT ON EU TREATY TALKS.

text.p: Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok said on Saturday a sudden rash of elections in the European Union had not swayed his determination to get an accord on a new draft treaty at the EU's June summit in Amsterdam.

"It will be hectic, never a dull moment," Kok told a news conference after a meeting of Europe's socialist leaders to prepare the ground for the June summit. "But this is not an invitation for the Dutch just to sit back and wait and see."

Kok, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency, has previously said that he would wait until after the May 1 general election in Britain -- where policy on Europe is dominating the campaign -- to announce whether a special EU summit would be held to clear the ground for the June meeting.
The EU summit, planned for June 16-17, is intended to overhaul the EU treaty for the day the bloc expands with up to 10 new countries.
Kok admitted on Saturday that politicians in Britain and France, which holds two rounds of parliamentary elections on May 25 and June 1, might have their hands tied in the poll run-up.
But he said the crucial moment in the revision of the treaty talks would be in the last days and even hours.
He said a final decision would be taken by May 15 on whether to hold the special meeting, already pencilled in for May 23.
The Dutch would also decide on the duration, the content and the formal nature of the extra meeting, he said. REUTER
